articles.title: In 2019, Scotland turned a retired lighthouse-supply ship into a 14-cabin floating hotel, opening its former bridge and hull to overnight guests
articles.summary: Explore the unique transformation of Fingal, a retired lighthouse-supply ship turned luxury floating hotel in Edinburgh. Experience maritime history with modern accommodations in a stunning waterfront setting.
articles.body: A ship once tasked with carrying lighthouse keepers, supplies, and maintenance crews around Scotland’s remote coastline began a very different chapter in 2019. After decades at sea and years in retirement, the vessel was transformed into Fingal, a luxury floating hotel permanently moored at Leith in Edinburgh.According to Fingal, the project turned a working vessel into a place where guests could sleep inside its former hull, dine aboard the ship and experience spaces shaped by its maritime past. The conversion also gave the vessel a new role in modern tourism while preserving its connection to its former work. Fingal’s story began in 1963, when the Northern Lighthouse Board (NLB) commissioned the vessel from Blythswood Shipbuilding Company in Glasgow. It was the last ship built by the yard. Registered in Leith, it spent about 30 years based in Oban before moving to Stromness in Orkney for its final six years of NLB service.From lighthouse tender to retirementFingal was not a regular passenger steamer. Instead, it assisted the Scottish lighthouse service by transporting personnel, equipment, and supplies to lighthouses far from the mainland. For lighthouse crews stationed in remote locations, the boat’s arrival could signal the end of a long separation from their families on the mainland.According to National Historic Ships, after retiring from Northern Lighthouse Board service in 2000, the vessel was sold to a private owner and renamed Windsor Castle. It remained in working order and was moored on the River Fal in Cornwall for the next 14 years. In 2014, the Royal Yacht Britannia Trust acquired the vessel. After a survey in Falmouth, it was towed to Leith, where plans were developed to convert the former lighthouse tender into a hotel. The Trust sought an additional source of revenue alongside the Royal Yacht Britannia, particularly because overnight accommodation was not permitted aboard the former royal yacht. Converting the lighthouse tender into a floating hotel provided a way to add hospitality facilities while preserving its maritime character.A ship rebuilt around its pastThe renovation involved gutting the ship and rebuilding its interior for hotel use while retaining its character as a former lighthouse tender. The new layout included bedrooms, restaurants, event spaces and elevators. The original funnel was removed to create space for two additional decks, with the upper deck accommodating the Lighthouse Restaurant and Bar and The Bridge, a private dining area. The upper section of the funnel was later relocated to the new deck to preserve the vessel's original appearance. Accommodation was added throughout the ship, with the final layout including main-deck cabins as well as larger rooms and suites created during the reconstruction. National Historic Ships records 14 cabins on the main deck, in addition to the larger accommodation and presidential suite elsewhere on the vessel.From working vessel to living heritageRecords show that Fingal opened to the public in January 2019, marking its full transformation from a lighthouse tender into a hotel. The Port of Leith is central to Edinburgh’s maritime history, giving Fingal a fitting waterfront setting. Beyond the hotel conversion, the design team added several details to enhance the guest experience. This is evident in the hull, which forms part of the accommodation, and in the nautical elements that link it to its previous life. Fingal was not a historic building in its original setting but a 73-metre-long ship that had spent years carrying people and supplies to remote lighthouses in Scotland.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2002, Houston built a runway for Boeing 747s using a concrete mix with 25% fly ash and 25% blast-furnace slag; test slabs reached 800 psi flexural strength in 90 days
articles.summary: Discover how Houston's George Bush Intercontinental Airport created a durable Boeing 747 runway using innovative concrete mixes with fly ash and slag, achieving exceptional structural performance.
articles.body: Runway concrete must do more than hold up aircraft. It must hold up to repeated heavy loads, resist moisture and be structurally sound for years, which makes the choice of cementitious materials very critical. Engineers at Houston’s George Bush Intercontinental Airport sought to meet those criteria while substituting half of the traditional cement with industrial by-products. Runway 15R-33L opened to air traffic on June 13, 2002. The runway was 10,000 feet long and 150 feet wide, designed to take Boeing 747s, Antonov 124s and other big aircraft. Its most remarkable feature, however, was hidden in the concrete: half of the cementitious material was composed of 25% Class F fly ash and 25% blast-furnace slag.In a 2003 Concrete International article, Shondeep L. Sarkar and Adil Godiwalla described the material properties and early performance of the runway concrete. After about eight months of service, they reported high strength, low permeability and a dense concrete structure.Houston required a new runwayThe original Runway 15R-33L was not intended for the size of the aircraft Houston expected. It was just 6,038 feet long and 100 feet broad. There was approximately 15 inches of full-depth asphalt over six inches of lime- stabilised subgrade. It was originally designed based on a DC-9 weighing roughly 121,000 pounds. The renovation extended it to 10,000 feet and widened it to 150 feet, allowing the runway to accommodate Boeing 747-class aircraft with maximum weights of around 875,000 pounds. The $100 million job, regarded as the largest runway whitetopping project at a U.S. airport at the time, was covered in a comprehensive ASCE project paper on the rebuilding of Runway 15R-33L.Whitetopping involves placing a new concrete pavement over an existing pavement structure rather than removing the entire roadway. For the runway upgrade, engineers milled about 8 inches of asphalt in the keel section before placing a 19-inch concrete overlay, allowing the existing pavement structure to remain part of the rebuilt runway. The finished concrete road was about 18 inches thick and covered some 300,000 square yards. It had to be designed to withstand bending forces generated by very large aeroplanes moving across the slab time and again.The ternary mix explainedA ternary blend is a mixture of three cementitious materials. The concrete at Bush Intercontinental had 50% Type I portland cement, 25% Class F fly ash and 25% Grade 120 blast-furnace slag by mass of the cementitious material. Fly ash is fine waste from the combustion of coal and blast-furnace slag is a by-product of iron manufacture. Both can participate in chemical reactions within the concrete and contribute to later age strength and a denser internal structure.The pavement was developed by the engineers of Houston for a flexural strength of 650 pounds per square inch. Trial batches were above the design target, reaching 800 psi in flexure at 90 days. Flexural strength is of special concern for pavements, since concrete slabs flex under the passage of aeroplane loads. A pavement mixture can therefore be evaluated not only by the compressive force it can withstand but also by its resistance to bending and cracking under repeated aircraft loads.The early field results were encouraging. The 2003 study found compressive strengths of roughly 6,730 to 9,790 psi in cores sampled after about eight months of service. Electrical testing indicated low permeability, while microscopic analysis found a dense concrete structure with little microcracking.The caution from Houston's other runwayNot every batch of concrete acted the same in Houston. Engineers later explored trouble at a critical runway intersection at neighbouring William P. Hobby Airport, which used a high-early-strength concrete mixture. ASCE performed a different study on the Hobby Airport runway restoration, indicating the service life of the previous pavement was decreased and the deterioration was mostly caused by the production of secondary ettringite crystals. Given the great emphasis on minimising runway closure time, fast strength development was a crucial feature of the original design.That experience did not suggest that high early-strength concrete was intrinsically unfit. It demonstrated that a pavement mix must be tailored to project conditions and priorities. Maximising early strength solves one problem of building but raises other problems of durability. Bush Intercontinental Runway went a different route. The ternary concrete was meant to develop significant strength at later ages while also offering low permeability. The fly ash and slag lowered the percentage of ordinary portland cement while maintaining the ability of the concrete to meet the structural requirements of the runway.There were tradeoffs. Cementitious blends with high proportions of fly ash and slag produce strength differently than plain portland-cement mixes; therefore, curing, building and opening needs need to be considered in design. A runway closure to allow concrete to gain strength presents a different problem than an emergency repair that must be opened within hours.What the results showHouston’s Runway 15R-33L demonstrated at full scale that a heavy-duty airport pavement could use a cementitious blend containing 50% industrial by-products. Trial concrete achieved 800 psi flexural strength at 90 days vs. a design basis of 650 psi. Initial field cores indicated satisfactory compressive strength and minimal permeability. It was not just a case of replacing Portland cement with waste materials. Engineers had to find a blend that was right for the aircraft loads, the construction process and the long-term durability needs.Houston’s experience at Hobby Airport offers a contrasting lesson: concrete designed for very rapid strength gain still needs to be evaluated for long-term durability. At Bush Intercontinental, the engineers instead used substantial amounts of fly ash and slag and designed the mix around the aircraft loads, construction requirements and expected service conditions.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Police in Moscow detained around 60 people at a rally organised by Russia's Kremlin-friendly Communist Party on Sunday, the party said, as protesters
articles.body: Police in Moscow detained around 60 people at a rally organised by Russia's Kremlin-friendly Communist Party on Sunday, the party said, as protesters called for political freedoms and fair elections.The detentions took place as the rally was ending, according to a statement from the party. Its Moscow branch said it was working to secure the release of those detained, most of whom were young people.The rally was held to mark the anniversary of the Kremlin's 1993 crackdown on a parliamentary uprising. According to the Telegram news channel Ostorozhno Novosti, protesters chanted slogans including "Freedom for political prisoners", "For fair elections" and "Down with the Tsar"., as quoted by AP.The gathering comes amid growing public frustration over the impact of Ukraine's intensifying drone attacks inside Russia. The strikes have targeted oil refineries and warehouses, causing fuel shortages and disrupting daily life, including in Moscow.The 1993 crisis followed a prolonged confrontation between then-President Boris Yeltsin and hard-line lawmakers opposed to his free-market reforms. Yeltsin ordered parliament dissolved, after which supporters of the lawmakers attempted to seize the state television broadcasting centre.Yeltsin then deployed the military, which shelled the parliament building with tanks. Authorities put the death toll at 123, while unofficial estimates said several hundred people were killed.Russia's Communist Party has remained one of the main forces in parliament since the 1990s. It has been led for more than three decades by Gennady Zyuganov, 82, a former Soviet official.Although the party has criticised some government policies during President Vladimir Putin's more than 25 years in power, it has avoided direct criticism of Putin and has consistently backed Russia's war in Ukraine.You use AI every day. articles.title: Australia funds more than $1 million to remove invasive weeds from a small island; the goal is to rebuild nesting habitat for seabirds
articles.summary: Australia funds more than $1 million in an ecological restoration project on South Islet in the Coral Sea Marine Park, where invasive weeds have reduced
articles.body: Australia funds more than $1 million in an ecological restoration project on South Islet in the Coral Sea Marine Park, where invasive weeds have reduced nesting areas for seabirds. The project involves removing invasive weeds and replanting native species to restore breeding habitat for seabirds.South Islet is part of the Willis Islets, commonly known as Willis Island, and is home to sooty terns, brown noddies and wedge-tailed shearwaters. According to Australian Marine Parks, H5 bird flu has been detected in Australia but has not been detected in the Coral Sea Marine Park. Parks Australia has already seen early signs of success, with seabirds using some of the cleared areas as nesting grounds.Why did Australia fund a $1 million-plus restoration on South IsletThe South Islet Ecological Restoration Project received an Australian Government investment of more than $1 million. Its aim is to restore nesting habitat for seabirds by removing invasive weeds and revegetating the island with native plant species. South Islet is in the Willis Islets, commonly known as Willis Island, in the Coral Sea Marine Park. It is a key breeding habitat for seabirds, including sooty terns, brown noddies and wedge-tailed shearwaters. It is also home to a staffed Bureau of Meteorology weather station.Invasive weeds have spread across about 35% of the island’s 4.8 hectares of vegetation. Mossman river grass, dwarf poinsettia and cat’s whiskers are among the invasive plants that have crowded out native vegetation and reduced the space available for seabird nesting.Restoring South Islet for nesting seabirdsIn May, an expedition team from Parks Australia, Indigenous Rangers from Mandubarra Indigenous Land and Sea Inc., and contractors spent 15 days working on South Islet with assistance from Bureau staff. The team removed weeds and trialled methods of revegetation. A second team returned for two weeks at the end of July to continue work. During the first trip, Parks Australia project lead Dr Roberta Johnson said staff spent more than 400 hours working among the birds. The team worked carefully around parent birds, chicks and eggs while removing the weeds by hand. The results were visible quickly, with sooty terns and brown noddies moving into some of the cleared areas to nest within hours.How have seabirds responded to the restored nesting areasDr Roberta Johnson said, “We cleared about 5 tonnes of weeds by hand, and we could actually see the results of our work in real time, with sooty terns and brown noddies moving into the nest in some cleared areas within hours”. When the second team returned two months later, more areas cleared of weeds were being used by nesting birds.The restoration will help safeguard seabird populations by protecting breeding sites while restoring the island’s ecosystem over the long term. The work will help prevent invasive weeds from spreading to other nearby islands.She said, “Our islands and reefs are home to unique species found nowhere else, but their ecosystems are delicate and vulnerable to threats ranging from H5 bird flu to climate change, so protecting them is a priority.”Where else is Parks Australia restoring seabird habitatSouth Islet is one of two ecological restoration projects underway on islands in the Coral Sea Marine Park. The other project is on Bird Islet at Wreck Reefs in the southern Coral Sea Marine Park. It is addressing areas of couch grass, green amaranth and nightshade that are threatening seabird nesting sites. The project focuses on removing invasive plants that compete with native vegetation and reduce space for breeding birds.The Coral Sea Marine Park is Australia’s largest marine park, covering nearly one million square kilometres of ocean off Queensland. articles.title: Kashmiri teacher fights period stigma, one village at a time
articles.summary: BARAMULLA: While most schools are quiet on Sundays, Aasima Jan heads into north Kashmir’s remote tribal villages to talk to girls and families about a
articles.body: BARAMULLA: While most schools are quiet on Sundays, Aasima Jan heads into north Kashmir’s remote tribal villages to talk to girls and families about a subject many still avoid: menstruation. For years, the 42-year-old govt school teacher has conducted awareness sessions on menstrual health, hygiene and stigma, while also persuading families to re-enrol children who have dropped out of school. Her efforts earned her J&K’s “Best Teacher Award” in 2023.Recruited in 2003, Aasima spent seven years teaching at a govt school in Bandipora. In 2009, she noticed many girls missing classes for up to a week during their periods. Some said their parents barred them from attending school while menstruating.The turning point came when she found a student crying over the shame surrounding periods. “It broke my heart. I felt a deep sense of responsibility and resolved to do something about it,” Aasima said. The next day, she began taking extra classes on menstruation and started counselling parents. “I tell girls this is natural. It is not a disease, but a sign that they are growing up,” she said. Attendance among girls improved.Aasima then moved beyond the classroom, conducting monthly awareness sessions at schools and visiting villages on Sundays and holidays. She continued the sessions even after her transfer to neighbouring Baramulla district. Her outreach expanded to remote areas such as Gurez and Uri, and to nomadic Gujjar and Bakerwal communities.Every Sunday, she picks a village, contacts local panches and sarpanches, and conducts sessions centred on “awareness, acceptance and action”. In remote areas, she often finds girls using cloth during periods while families, including mothers, are reluctant to discuss menstruation. Aasima spends her own money buying sanitary pads to distribute during visits, while explaining their use and disposal.Her social media page, with around 40,000 followers, also promotes menstrual health and other social causes. For Aasima, the biggest reward is seeing students continue the work by spreading awareness and positivity about menstrual health.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Gurgaon water demand may rise 52% by 2031, supply gap met by tubewells, HC told
articles.summary: Gurgaon water demand may rise 52% to 1,170 MLD by 2031, Punjab and Haryana HC told; city bridges a 100 MLD gap via tubewells as groundwater falls.
articles.body: Gurgaon: City’s water requirement is likely to rise by around 52% in the next five years, from about 770 million litres a day (MLD) now to 1,170 MLD by 2031. The city already faces a gap of around 100 MLD between demand and GMDA’s treatment capacity, according to written submissions by environmental activist Sunil Singh in a groundwater case before the Punjab and Haryana High Court.The high court considered the submissions at its Oct 1 hearing. It has directed GMDA CEO P C Meena to convene a meeting of govt agencies and other stakeholders on Monday to examine the city’s worsening groundwater situation, and the outcome is to be placed before the court on Oct 8. The court has recorded that groundwater levels in different parts of the city are nearly 40 metres below ground level. It has asked authorities to examine the issue in detail and to explore specifically whether groundwater extraction can be discontinued in areas where GMDA water supply is available.GMDA’s two water treatment plants have a combined capacity of about 670 MLD, against present potable water demand of around 770 MLD. The remaining roughly 100 MLD is being met through tubewells operated by MCG and private builders, the submissions said.The state has drawn up a plan to raise treatment capacity in phases to around 1,170 MLD between 2026 and 2029, to meet the projected 2031 demand. Officials had told the state govt that several parts of the city were already connected to the GMDA network, while work was planned to expand coverage in other sectors.The immediate concern, however, is the dependence on groundwater to bridge the present gap. Gurgaon district extracts around 1,185 MLD of groundwater a year against an annual extractable resource of about 557 MLD, putting the stage of groundwater extraction at 212.77%, the submissions said.They also point to the loss of natural areas that allow groundwater to recharge. TERI data cited in the matter shows Gurgaon district’s built-up area rose from 189.67 sq km in 2007 to 393.54 sq km in 2019, and was projected to reach 518.86 sq km in 2025.Over the same period, the area under water bodies fell from 55.25 sq km to just 5.34 sq km in 2019. The city thus faces two linked problems: groundwater is being extracted faster than it is replenished, while urban growth is pushing up demand.A GMDA survey cited in the submissions examined 1,216 water bodies during earlier proceedings before National Green Tribunal. It found that 390 had been completely destroyed and were not retrievable, while the remaining 826 were considered retrievable in 2017.The survey identified 305 existing public water bodies covering around 393 acres, and more than 140 natural low-lying areas covering about 412 acres, that could be restored to help recharge groundwater.The submissions also flag continuing pressure on these areas. Fifty-three water bodies covering about 78 acres face dumping, levelling, encroachment, construction or changes in land use. Another 130, covering around 132 acres, are affected or threatened by untreated sewage, industrial effluent or other wastewater.A further 123 water bodies under the combined ownership of govt authorities have been identified for demarcation, fencing and cleaning to improve groundwater recharge, but the exercise has not been carried out, the submissions said. They propose restoring these water bodies, their catchments and feeder channels through a committee under the supervision of a former Supreme Court or high court judge.The submissions also point to treated wastewater as a way of reducing Gurgaon’s dependence on fresh water. HSPCB records cited in them show around 300 MLD of wastewater reaching the Dhanwapur STP location in Jan 2026. An irrigation network capable of using about 300 MLD of treated wastewater has already been laid, but it is not being fully used because not all the treated water meets the prescribed standards.The state has approved reuse of treated wastewater from four major STPs, including Dhanwapur, for irrigating around 28,000 acres at an estimated cost of Rs 282.13 crore. The submissions propose a “Zero Discharge/Maximum Reuse” system under which untreated sewage and industrial effluent would not be allowed to enter stormwater drains, natural water bodies, open land or groundwater.The submissions separately propose stopping groundwater extraction through borewells in Gurgaon, whether registered, permitted or unregistered. They call for existing borewells to be identified, geo-tagged and sealed in a time-bound manner. Existing permissions and NOCs for extraction would stay suspended during the exercise, with no new borewell, renewal of permission or increase in permitted extraction quantity allowed.They also question whether further construction or an increase in development should be allowed unless authorities can first demonstrate an assured and sustainable source of water that does not depend on groundwater.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Gurgaon | Silver Rate in Gurgaon | Bank Holidays in Gurgaon | Public Holidays in Gurgaon | Gurgaon AQI | Weather in Gurgaon | Petrol Price in Gurgaon | Diesel Price in Gurgaon | CNG Price in Gurgaon | LPG Price in GurgaonStay updated with the latest Gurgaon news. articles.title: Malena Tudi to address viral claims about her divorce from Nmplol after months away from internet
articles.summary: Malena Tudi is preparing to return to Twitch to address what she calls misinformation surrounding her divorce from fellow streamer Nick “Nmplol” Polom.
articles.body: Malena Tudi is preparing to return to Twitch to address what she calls misinformation surrounding her divorce from fellow streamer Nick “Nmplol” Polom. After staying away from the internet for months, Tudi said she plans to go live on her personal Twitch channel when she feels ready to explain her side of the story. She said the decision is not about creating content but about protecting her self-respect, especially after online claims began affecting her real life. However, she has not revealed when the livestream will happen.Malena Tudi plans Twitch stream to address claims about her divorce from NmplolTudi explained that she had hoped to disappear from the internet and continue her life away from the attention. However, she said a “fictional label” placed on her online has started affecting her personal life.According to Tudi, childhood friends have asked whether certain claims about her are true, while she has also been recognized and questioned in public. This made it difficult for her to completely move on from the controversy.She said she does not want to be remembered as someone she believes she is not. Tudi stressed that the situation goes beyond online content and is instead connected to her self-respect.The streamer also spoke about the role therapy has played in her life. She said she has spent a decade dealing with trauma and believes she owes it to her younger self to protect her now. While reopening the situation is difficult, she said she is no longer afraid and wants to remain in control of her own actions.Malena Tudi says she wants to clear misinformation without returning to court dramaTudi said she will eventually go live on her personal Twitch channel to clear up misinformation, but she does not know exactly when. She explained that she wants to make sure she handles the situation properly because she does not want to be dragged back into the judicial system or an ongoing cycle of negativity and manipulation.Her decision comes after months of online discussion surrounding her reported split from Nmplol. YouTuber Henry Resilient previously claimed that the pair had separated and shared transcripts that he said came from their divorce trial. articles.title: More than optics: Akhilesh’s MLC gambit targets BJP, courts upper castes
articles.summary: Akhilesh Yadav swaps SP MLC nominees for BJP rebel Sanjayan Tripathi and hopeful Akash Agarwal, aiming to dent BJP and broaden PDA to upper castes.
articles.body: Lucknow: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav’s decision to replace party nominees with BJP rebels and ticket hopefuls for the MLC polls may appear to be a clever attempt to embarrass the BJP. Yet, beyond the optics, the move underscores SP’s attempt to project its PDA coalition as an inclusive social alliance with space for upper castes as well.On Saturday, the SP chief replaced Kamlesh Yadav – who was declared the SP candidate from Gorakhpur-Faizabad Teachers constituency - with BJP rebel Sanjayan Tripathi. Similarly, SP candidate from Agra Graduate seat Prakash Chandra Gupta was replaced by Akash Agarwal who was seeking a ticket from the BJP. The move, SP strategists say, was aimed at hitting the rival BJP on more than one front.To begin with, the idea behind inducting Sanjayan Tripathi and Akash Agarwal was to demolish BJP’s claims that SP’s PDA plank - which originally focused on Pichhde (backward classes), Dalit and alpsankhyaks (minorities) – was a gateway to politics of caste divide where upper castes have no role. It was this charge of the BJP that prompted Akhilesh to announce that the letters ‘PD’ in PDA stood for Pandits and upper castes.“Now Sanjayan Tripathi - who happens to be a Brahmin - has been accommodated by SP on a seat vacated by party nominee Kamlesh Yadav who hails from OBC community. Is there anything more needed to explain SP’s commitment towards everyone who is ‘Peedit’ because of BJP,” said a senior SP functionary associated with drafting party strategies.At the same time, SP nominee Prakash Chandra Gupta being replaced by Akash Agarwal too has sent across the message that other upper caste communities, which may not have been known for traditionally backing SP in polls, were also equally welcomed, he said.What actually paved way for Sanjayan Tripathi’s entry into SP was his recent emotional videos that went viral on social media where he was seen taking off the BJP flag from the bonnet mast of his SUV recalling how he had served the BJP selflessly for so many years and how his supporters now wanted him to take a stand on being neglected and sidelined.Political observers believe that what added to Tripathi’s appeal was the fact that he was seeking MLC ticket from (Gorakhpur – Faizabad Teachers seat) a region where Akhilesh had accused the BJP govt of targeting Brahmins and coined the phase “unhen hata nahi bhata, tilak nahi lubhata” (someone does not approve of haata and tilak) during political addresses to target chief minister Yogi Adityanath.Political observers are of the view that Akhilesh’s ‘Haata’ jibe apparently refers to Tiwari Hata in Gorakhpur – the residence of influential Brahmin face Harishankar Tiwari. articles.title: Judo 2026 World Championships: Koga and Yusifov Strike Gold on Opening Day in Baku
articles.summary: Wakana Koga claimed her first world title at -48kg, defeating Assunta Scutto in the final. At -60kg, home favourite Ahmad Yusifov came from behind to beat Sh...
articles.body:
Welcome to Baku, Azerbaijan, where new legends will rise to claim their red back patches at the Baku World Judo Championships 2026.

At -48kg, Italy's Assunta SCUTTO claimed her place in the final for the third time in a row with impressive judo all morning. Her third time in a World final, but could she take the gold for a second time?

Meeting her there was Japan's KOGA Wakana . The Japanese judoka was in fantastic form, with high quality judo throughout the day. KOGA already has a World bronze and silver, would this be the year to claim the missing gold? With every contest, she looked increasingly assured, carrying real momentum into the final.

In the final the two experienced judoka clashed. It was a tightly fought contest, with neither judoka giving much away, before KOGA seized her opportunity on the ground. Calm under pressure, she converted the opportunity decisively to bring the contest to an emphatic close. It was KOGA who walked away crowned the World Champion. A breakthrough moment for the Japanese star.

The great spirit from the fans, the energy that was coming in came into me and I managed to achieve better because of the support from the fans in the arena.

Azerbaijan National Olympic Committee Secretary General Mr Azer ALIYEV awarded the medals.

In the -60kg, Ahmad YUSIFOV secured his first time in a World final here in his home nation. An impressive feat for the local favourite who was looking to claim his red backpatch. With the Baku crowd firmly behind him, the stage was set for a huge home final.

Facing him was Kazakhstan's Sherzod DAVLATOV , also in his first World final. Would DAVLATOV secure himself a place in history? The Kazakh had looked composed and dangerous throughout the day.

YUSIFOV rose to the occasion in front of a passionate home crowd to claim victory. With the pressure at its highest, YUSIFOV came from a score down, sparking huge celebrations and creating what is sure to be one of the standout moments of this World Championships.

International Judo Federation Executive Committee Member Mr Timur KEMELL awarded the medals.

There are always good things in my mind, I wouldn't have lost a contest in front of the audience here and now I'm feeling great.

What an incredible first day here in Baku. Join us tomorrow in the land of fire.

articles.title: Akhilesh promises job guarantee for govt posts if SP returns in 2027
articles.summary: Akhilesh Yadav pledges job guarantee for govt posts if SP wins UP in 2027, promising transparent recruitment, annual exam calendar, anti-leak force and end to outsourcing.
articles.body: Lucknow: Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav on Sunday promised a job guarantee for govt posts if the party returns to power in the state in 2027, outlining a recruitment overhaul that includes a transparent process, an annual examination calendar and a special force to curb question paper leaks.Speaking at the ‘PDA Sankalp–Teacher and Aspirant Dialogue with Akhilesh Ji’ programme at Ram Manohar Lohia Park in Gomti Nagar, Akhilesh addressed students, job aspirants and parents, saying recruitment examinations would be conducted with strict safeguards and that those responsible for leaks would face strong action.“Examination papers do not merely get leaked; they are made to leak,” he said, alleging deliberate wrongdoing behind repeated leak incidents. He said a future SP govt would impose firm restrictions to prevent leaks and ensure accountability through stringent punitive measures.Akhilesh also announced that the outsourcing system would be abolished permanently, promising regular, permanent jobs in its place. He said teachers would receive better training facilities and support, linking improvements in education administration to wider employment outcomes.Emphasising the relationship between jobs and economic growth, he said no economy could progress without livelihood opportunities. He claimed young people were struggling to find work despite qualifications because of a gap between education and employment planning.The SP chief called for reforms in universities, alleging several campuses had become centres of ideological influence and factional groups, and said changes were necessary to improve institutional functioning.During the programme, representatives of coaching institutes flagged recruitment delays, vacant posts and the pressures faced by candidates preparing for competitive examinations.Akhilesh thanked organisers and recalled that Ram Manohar Lohia Park was developed during the SP govt led by Mulayam Singh Yadav, claiming it was built across five hectares without cutting trees, which were relocated. He cited the Agra-Lucknow Expressway as a key project from his tenure and criticised the BJP govt’s development claims for Gorakhpur and Varanasi.Referring to Lucknow, he said the city had grown as a hub for information technology and education, pointing to HCL and the IIIT campus, and said laptops distributed during the SP govt were still in use.‘Alliance focused on winning, not seat sharing’Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Tuesday said the opposition alliance should prioritise winning elections over bargaining about seat-sharing among partners. He said the key issue was not the number of seats each constituent would contest or which party would get which constituency, but how the alliance could secure victory. Reiterating the message, Akhilesh urged parties to focus on a unified strategy rather than internal negotiations. He said an alliance win would rise above individual party interests and reflect a collective effort to stop communalism from gaining ground again.
